data.title: Robbins LLP Urges RYDE Stockholders Who Lost Money Investing in Ryde Group Ltd to Contact the Firm for Information About Leading the Class Action
data.description:
Robbins LLP Urges RYDE Stockholders Who Lost Money Investing in Ryde Group Ltd to Contact the Firm for Information About Leading the Class Action

Shareholder rights law firm Robbins LLP reminds investors that a class action was filed on behalf of all persons and entities who purchased or otherwise acquired Ryde Group Ltd (NYSE: RYDE) securities between March 6, 2024 and September 11, 2024, inclusive (the "Class Period"). RYDE’s claimed “vision is to become a 'Super mobility app' where multiple mobility tools can be accessed and function seamlessly out of a single app, offering ultimate convenience and reliability for our customers.”

The complaint alleges that RYDE experienced a sudden collapse in stock price following a dramatic yet illusory run-up orchestrated by a fraudulent stock promotion scheme.

Investors who suffered significant losses during the Class Period may be eligible to participate in the lawsuit and should contact Robbins LLP prior to the November 9, 2026, lead plaintiff deadline.

Listen to our podcast.

Why Was RYDE Sued?

The complaint alleges that, during the Class Period, defendants failed to disclose to investors that:

(1) RYDE was the subject of a fraudulent stock promotion scheme involving social media-based misinformation and impersonated financial professionals;
(2) insiders and/or affiliates used offshore or nominee accounts to facilitate the coordinated dumping of shares during a price inflation campaign;
(3) RYDE’s public statements and risk disclosures omitted any mention of the false rumors and artificial trading activity driving the stock price; and
(4) as a result of the foregoing, Defendants’ positive statements about the Company’s business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis.

Why Did RYDE Stock Drop?

Plaintiff alleges that in the weeks and months leading up to the collapse, RYDE’s share price surged from an initial public offering (“IPO”) price of $4.00 to an all-time high of $22.49 despite no fundamental changes to the Company or news to justify the spike. Investigations and public reports have since revealed that RYDE utilized social media to orchestrate an illicit “pump-and- dump” promotion scheme to defraud investors. These reports detail how impersonators claiming to be legitimate financial advisors touted RYDE in online forums, chat groups, and through social media posts with sensational but baseless claims to create a buying frenzy among retail investors.

However, on September 11, 2024, RYDE’s share price abruptly crashed approximately 75%, to $5.50. Since then, the Company’s share price has rapidly declined to approximately $0.50.

Who May Be Eligible to Participate in the RYDE Class Action?

The lawsuit seeks to represent investors who purchased or otherwise acquired Ryde Group Ltd common stock between March 6, 2024 and September 11, 2024. Investors who suffered losses during that period may have legal rights under the federal securities laws.

What Is a Lead Plaintiff?

The lead plaintiff is a court-appointed investor who represents the interests of all class members throughout the litigation. Shareholders who wish to lead the case should contact Robbins LLP before the November 9, 2026, lead plaintiff deadline.

Serving as lead plaintiff is not required to share in any potential recovery. Investors who do not seek appointment may remain absent class members if the case proceeds and later resolves successfully.

Does It Cost Anything to Participate?

No. Robbins LLP represents investors on a contingency fee basis.

Why Robbins LLP?

A recognized leader in shareholder rights litigation, Robbins LLP has helped restore more than $2 billion in value to shareholders and secured some of the largest recoveries in shareholder derivative litigation history.

"Companies have an obligation to provide investors with complete and accurate information so that markets can function fairly and efficiently," said Brian J. Robbins, Founding Partner of Robbins LLP.

To be notified if a class action against Ryde Group Ltd settles or to receive free alerts when corporate executives engage in wrongdoing, sign up for Stock Watch today.

Contact Robbins LLP

Investors seeking additional information about the Ryde Group Ltd securities class action may contact Robbins LLP by submitting an inquiry, emailing attorney Aaron Dumas, Jr., or calling (800) 350-6003.

Attorney Advertising. Past results do not guarantee a similar outcome.

data.title: CORRECTING and REPLACING Tekion, Increase, and Core Bank Partner to Bring Industry-First Embedded Banking to Automotive Retail
data.description:
CORRECTING and REPLACING Tekion, Increase, and Core Bank Partner to Bring Industry-First Embedded Banking to Automotive Retail

Tekion Spend offers the first fully-featured bank account native to an automotive dealer management system.

Please replace the release issued September 23, 2026, with the following corrected version due to multiple revisions.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260923757647/en/

The updated release reads:

TEKION, INCREASE, AND CORE BANK PARTNER TO BRING INDUSTRY-FIRST EMBEDDED BANKING TO AUTOMOTIVE RETAIL

Tekion Spend offers the first fully-featured bank account native to an automotive dealer management system.

Tekion, Increase, and Core Bank today announced embedded banking inside Automotive Retail Cloud (ARC). Built from the ground up as AI-native, ARC unifies all departments across more than 2,000 dealerships today. Tekion Spend, built on Increase in partnership with Core Bank, provides the first fully embedded banking solution designed for automotive dealerships.

Automotive dealerships are operationally complex businesses. Every year, a single dealership makes hundreds of thousands of payments to various suppliers, vendors, and customers. Until now, dealerships have had to make those payments outside of the software platform they use to run the rest of their business. Dealership staff have to manage an external bank account and print thousands of checks annually to make payments. Most still reconcile payments manually in their dealership management system at month end.

Tekion Spend solves this by embedding banking directly into ARC. Dealerships can now:

  • Open a fully-featured, FDIC-insured bank account in their name
  • Store and earn money on their deposits
  • Send money over any US payment rail and see exactly where it is at every moment
  • Reconcile payments in real-time
  • Manage every rooftop from one account

Increase makes this all possible via API, offering bare-metal infrastructure that gives Tekion full access to the Federal Reserve's data and capabilities, in partnership with Core Bank. Increase provides accounts and scaled accounts payable for Tekion Spend.

Accounts payable is the first step in Tekion’s larger plans for embedded banking. Dealerships move billions annually just to manage their floorplans. They also move money in service, sales, finance and insurance, and payroll. Today, each of those flows ends in a separate portal. Through Tekion Spend with banking powered by Increase, dealerships can soon manage the vast majority of their funds' flows from within ARC.

“Tekion Spend gives automotive dealerships a fully-featured bank account inside their existing system of record,” said Jamie Fox, GM of Fintech at Tekion. “It sees the invoice, the payment, and the ledger entry as one object rather than three systems reporting to each other after the fact. This is a natural step in Tekion’s mission to deliver end-to-end service for automotive retail.”

“Increase exists to help ambitious technology companies build great financial products,” said Jack Flintermann Reed, Head of Product at Increase. “We help our users get to market faster than they imagined possible. Prior to building the full product that’s launching today, Tekion built an initial working prototype on Increase APIs in less than three weeks.”

“Tekion has built an impressive platform and has a deep understanding of the operational needs of today’s dealerships,” said Lindsay Borgeson, President of Core X. “We are excited to partner with Tekion to bring even greater value to the automotive retail market and give their customers the confidence that comes from having their dealership funds held with a trusted, regulated financial institution. We believe this partnership will deliver meaningful value to dealerships and are thrilled about what we can accomplish together.”

Tekion Spend is available to US ARC dealerships beginning in Q4.

Tekion Spend banking products and services are provided by Core Bank, Member FDIC. Technology services are provided by Increase Technologies, Inc. Tekion is not a bank.

About Tekion

Tekion is redefining automotive retail with its end-to-end AI-native, platform purpose-built for the industry. By embedding AI into every workflow, Tekion delivers intelligent automation, real-time insights, and advanced decision support - driving efficiency, revenue, and modern consumer experiences. As the first and fastest cloud-native platform for automotive, Tekion brings OEMs, dealers, partners, and consumers together through its revolutionary suite: Automotive Retail Cloud (ARC) for retailers, Automotive Enterprise Cloud (AEC) for manufacturers and large automotive enterprises, and Automotive Partner Cloud (APC) for technology and industry partners. With AI-powered, cloud-native technology, Tekion enables the most seamless, transparent, and profitable retail experiences in the industry. For more information, visit www.tekion.com.

About Increase

Increase offers API-first banking for ambitious technology companies. Companies like Coast, Gusto, and Ramp rely on Increase technology to process more than $500B annualized in payments, card transactions, and loans. Increase built its own bank core technology from scratch: it’s transparent, reliable, and flexible so users can build great financial products on top. Increase has offered banking infrastructure since 2020 and introduced Increase Bank, Member FDIC in 2026. Learn more at increase.com.

About Core Bank

Core X, a division of Core Bank, is a technology-forward, solutions-driven financial institution built for fintech and Vertical SaaS companies that need more from their banking partner. Core X delivers a differentiated partnership built around speed to market, deep compliance expertise, strong risk management, and strategic support. Through our managed compliance model, partners can focus on growing their businesses while Core Bank provides the regulatory oversight and banking expertise to scale responsibly. Connect at www.corebank.com/core-x-partner-banking

Media Contacts

Tekion: Marylou Hastert, press@tekion.com

Increase: Jeff Sorensen, press@increase.com

Core Bank: Tami Matousek, marketing@corebank.com

data.title: 'I HAD EVERY OPTION,' SAYS RADIATION ONCOLOGIST WHO CHOSE PROTON THERAPY AT PROCURE FOR HIS OWN PROSTATE CANCER
data.description:
'I HAD EVERY OPTION,' SAYS RADIATION ONCOLOGIST WHO CHOSE PROTON THERAPY AT PROCURE FOR HIS OWN PROSTATE CANCER

'I HAD EVERY OPTION,' SAYS RADIATION ONCOLOGIST WHO CHOSE PROTON THERAPY AT PROCURE FOR HIS OWN PROSTATE CANCER

PR Newswire

SOMERSET, N.J., Sept. 25, 2026

SOMERSET, N.J., Sept. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As ProCure Proton Therapy Center continues health education efforts during National Prostate Cancer Awareness Month, the provider is highlighting a patient story with a distinctive vantage point.

Edward Soffen, M.D., underwent proton therapy treatments at ProCure earlier this year for his own prostate cancer. He also happens to be a radiation oncologist with expertise in a full range of radiation therapy modalities, including proton therapy.

"I had every option available, and I could have chosen any provider in the world," said Dr. Soffen. "When I asked myself what made the most sense for my own body, I applied my 30-plus years of experience to my own situation, exploring six different treatment options. I landed on protons as the one clear choice—and I have zero regrets about that decision."

A prostate cancer specialist for more than 30 years, Dr. Soffen has personally performed nearly every radiation technique for the disease, including CyberKnife, radioactive seed implants, high-dose-rate brachytherapy, conventional radiation with IMRT, and protons, matching the modality to each patient's unique situation. Because his own cancer was caught early and confined to the prostate, protons were an option. He chose them for the same reason he recommends them to certain patients: the dose goes to the tumor and stops, sparing surrounding healthy tissue.

Choosing protons narrowed the field. Choosing where to receive them was the more personal decision. Dr. Soffen knows the proton centers in the region and beyond, and he could have been treated at any of them. He chose the one where he practices, alongside colleagues he has watched treat thousands of complex cases with a personalized approach he has seen from the inside for years. When it was his turn to be the patient, he wanted the ProCure team.

"Dr. Soffen has spent his career helping patients weigh exactly these choices, and when the diagnosis was his own, he trusted that process—and our team," said Brian Chon, M.D., Medical Director at ProCure. "That's the kind of confidence we strive to earn from every patient."

"I've spent my career on the other side of this conversation, and I know how rare it is to find a team that gets both the physics and the person right," said Dr. Soffen. "I trusted ProCure with my patients for years. Trusting them with myself was the easiest decision in the whole process."

About ProCure Proton Therapy Center
ProCure Proton Therapy Center in Somerset, NJ, opened in March 2012 as the tri-state region's first proton therapy facility, treating a range of cancers including diseases of the prostate, breast, lung, brain, head and neck, and gastrointestinal system, as well as sarcomas and many pediatric cases. Using the most advanced radiation treatment available, ProCure has treated more than 8,000 patients overall, including 750+ pediatric patients coming from the U.S. and abroad, and enables many cancer patients to choose a non-surgical treatment personalized to their medical needs and lifestyles, often with fewer side effects and less downtime—giving them more freedom to enjoy what matters most in their lives. For more information, visit ProCure.com.

data.title: Wheat Futures Down After U.S.-China Has Quiet Finish — Daily Grain Highlights
data.description:
By Kirk Maltais 




  -- Wheat for December delivery fell 0.4% to $7.04 a bushel on the Chicago Board of Trade Friday, with traders following through on selling after the U.S.-China summit in Washington didn't result in new announcements of Chinese agricultural purchases. 



  -- Corn for December delivery rose 0.2% to $5.28 3/4 a bushel. 



  -- Soybeans for November rose 0.2% to $13.20 a bushel. 





  HIGHLIGHTS 





  Light on Results: CBOT grain futures fell after President Trump and Chinese leader Xi's summit in Washington wrapped up with no new announcements on agricultural purchases. 



  "Bull markets need to be fed daily, and no fresh news means a price correction to the downside has started," said Naomi Blohm of Total Farm Marketing in a note. Blohm said that "any correction lower will be short-lived, due to overall smaller grain supplies globally," making the lower prices a potential buying opportunity for traders, as evidenced by a paring of losses as the day progressed. 



  Losing Steam: Losses in CBOT grains pared midday, turning positive late after the downward momentum earlier in the day ran out of gas. [We view] the early morning decline as momentum-driven rather than a deterioration in grain fundamentals," said AgResource in a note. The firm adds that wet weather in the Corn Belt and conflicts overseas continue to be factors supporting grain prices longer term. 





  INSIGHT 





  Remaining Tension: The U.S.-China summit held in Washington ended with a general lack of news, even though USTR Jamieson Greer said that substantive announcements out of the summit are coming Monday. 



  But the general sentiment following the summit is that the relationship between the U.S. and China remains saddled with "deep distrust," said analysts with Capital Economics in a note. "While the two sides can temporarily contain tensions, they remain at an impasse on many of their most important disagreements." 



  Next Steps: The USDA is scheduled to release its quarterly stocks report covering the third quarter on Sept. 30. Traders see the report as an indicator for how old-crop demand fared. 



  "This report hasn't brought much volatility in the last decade-plus, though it has produced bearish soybean moves in each of the last five years," said Matt Zeller of StoneX in a note. Attention is expected to grow next week, with traders right now focusing on implications from the Trump-Xi summit. 





  AHEAD 





  -- The USDA is scheduled to release its weekly Grain Export Inspections Report at 11 a.m. EDT Monday. 



  -- The USDA is due to release its weekly Crop Progress Report at 4 p.m. EDT Monday. 



  -- The USDA is scheduled to release its monthly agricultural prices report at 3 p.m. EDT Tuesday.

data.title: Spartan College of Aeronautics and Technology and National Aviation Academy of Azerbaijan sign Cooperation Agreement to Train Azerbaijan's Next Generation of Aviation Maintenance Technicians
data.description:
Spartan College of Aeronautics and Technology and National Aviation Academy of Azerbaijan sign Cooperation Agreement to Train Azerbaijan's Next Generation of Aviation Maintenance Technicians

Agreement will prepare students from Azerbaijan for aviation maintenance careers through Spartan's hybrid Aviation Maintenance Technology program, with hands-on training delivered at its Denver-area campus in Broomfield, Colorado, USA.

Spartan College of Aeronautics and Technology (Spartan) and National Aviation Academy (NAA) of Azerbaijan have announced a cooperation agreement. Under the agreement, students from Azerbaijan will enroll in Spartan's Aviation Maintenance Technology hybrid program, which leads to an AAS degree awarded by Spartan's Tulsa, Oklahoma campus upon successful completion.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260925757404/en/

Pictured: Robert Polston, CEO of Spartan Education Group and Rector Arif Pashayev of the National Aviation Academy of Azerbaijan

“Developing modern aviation is important to the future of Azerbaijan,” said Rector Arif Pashayev of NAA. “In addition to scientific research and integration of new technologies, training a qualified work force is central to our efforts. Being able to provide not only excellent vocational training but an international experience with a partner like Spartan is an exciting opportunity for our students.”

The AMT program combines 13 months of online coursework with interactive content and 8 months of practical hands-on lab training. Under a consortium agreement between Spartan's Tulsa and Broomfield campuses, the practical lab portion will take place in Broomfield, Colorado. There, students will work directly on aircraft, engines, and components under the guidance of experienced, FAA certified instructors. After graduation, the students will be eligible to sit for the FAA Airframe and Powerplant examinations. Upon returning to Baku, the students will spend approximately 2 months in a State Civil Aviation Agency (Azerbaijan) conversion course at NAA followed by additional type rating training, that is not affiliated with any of Spartan’s curriculum or training.

"Airlines that recognize the strategic value of a reliable pipeline of certificated aviation maintenance technicians will be better positioned to sustain long-term growth,” said Robert Polston, CEO of Spartan Education Group. “Our cooperation agreement with NAA represents an important step, beginning with the training of technicians currently employed by Silk Way Group and AZAL. This partnership reflects a mutual commitment to long-term, strategic relationships that strengthen the Azerbaijani aviation workforce.”

“This initiative is essential to achieving our ambitions to further develop and enhance the Azerbaijan aviation sector, an important part of our transportation infrastructure,” said Rashad Nabiev, Minister of Digital Development and Transport of Azerbaijan.

“This cooperation will play a significant role in developing and expanding international aviation education in Azerbaijan, training a new generation of aviation professionals,” said Farhad Azima, Founder and CEO of ALG Transportation Group, who played an important role in bringing these two partners together.

Additionally, supporting this initiative and in attendance at the signing were Ambassador Hafiz Pashayev, Rector of ADA University and Deputy Minister of Science and Education Firudin Gurbanov.

Representing Silk Way Group and Azerbaijan Airlines (AZAL) were CEO Zaur Akhundov and COO Onno Pietersma and Chairman Samir Rzayev and Chief Technical Director Scott McConnell, respectively. Together, Silk Way Group and AZAL are sponsoring the first cohort of students.

And representing Spartan were CEO Robert Polston, EVP of Strategy and Development Daniel Bregman and Board of Directors Member Capt. David Bourne.

The first cohort, of sixty-one students, is participating in the ADA University intensive English language preparation course with a technical aviation focus. After enrolling at Spartan College of Aeronautics and Technology the students will begin their AMT studies on November 16, 2026.

About Spartan College

Established in 1928, Spartan College of Aeronautics and Technology is a system of three schools with four locations and has trained over 100,000 pilots and technicians. Campuses are located in the following areas: Tulsa, OK; Los Angeles, CA; Inland Empire, CA; and Denver, CO. Spartan students have come from across the United States and over 40 countries. To learn more and for consumer information, location of training, school licensing and accreditation visit www.Spartan.edu. Programs, credential levels, technology, and scheduling options vary by campus and are subject to change. Third-party certifications and employment opportunities are not guaranteed. Financing options are available for those who apply and qualify. Administrative office: Spartan Education Group, LLC, 1 N. Franklin St., Suite 2125, Chicago, IL 60606

About National Aviation Academy of Azerbaijan

The National Aviation Academy (NAA) of Azerbaijan, based in Baku, is Azerbaijan's leading higher education institution for civil aviation and aerospace. It was founded in 1992 as the National Aviation Centre and took its current name in 1994. NAA offers bachelor's, master's and doctoral programs in pilot training, air traffic control, aircraft maintenance and engineering, avionics, and airport and logistics management. It operates under ICAO standards and a working arrangement with the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA). Learn more at naa.edu.az.

Spartan Education Group, LLC

data.title: ULTRALOQ Launches Next-Generation Smart Lock Collection: Refining Home Entry with Natural, Intelligent and Trusted Access Solutions
data.description:
ULTRALOQ Launches Next-Generation Smart Lock Collection: Refining Home Entry with Natural, Intelligent and Trusted Access Solutions

ULTRALOQ Launches Next-Generation Smart Lock Collection: Refining Home Entry with Natural, Intelligent and Trusted Access Solutions

PR Newswire

LAS VEGAS and SAN JOSE, Calif., Sept. 25, 2026

New Bolt Mission, Bolt Pro, and Latch 5 Pro give homeowners a choice between precise, hands-free UWB entry and tap-to-unlock digital keys 

LAS VEGAS and SAN JOSE, Calif., Sept. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ULTRALOQ, a best-selling smart lock brand under Xthings, a global leader in IoT solutions, today announced the launch and availability of its next-generation smart lock collection, built to redefine access and provide customers with a wide range of effortless entry experiences that best suit their lifestyle.

The collection includes ULTRALOQ Bolt Mission, unveiled as the industry's first ultra-wideband (UWB) enabled smart lock, featuring precise, hands-free approach-to-unlock functionality. Joining Bolt Mission are the ULTRALOQ Bolt Pro and ULTRALOQ Latch 5 Pro which are the first multi-model line of Aliro-Certified smart locks that empowers users to leverage their phone as their key through Apple Wallet or Samsung Wallet credentials. 

The latest ULTRALOQ models arrive at a time when digital wallets and standardized access credentials are reshaping how consumers expect to access their homes and other everyday assets. For the new collection, ULTRALOQ leverages UWB to enable precise, intent-aware entry to the home and Aliro, the open mobile-access standard developed by the Connectivity Standards Alliance with support from leading mobile ecosystems including Apple, Google and Samsung. With Aliro, ULTRALOQ brings the familiar wallet-based experience consumers already use for payments and increasingly digital car keys to the front door.

All three lock models are Matter Certified and compatible with leading smart home platforms, including Apple Home, Google Home and more, allowing users to incorporate the lock into their broader smart home experience. Bolt Pro and Latch 5 Pro also integrate with Samsung SmartThings, enabling more home-wide automations triggered by lock activity, such as turning on lights or adjusting the thermostat when the door unlocks. Household members can have their own Digital Key in Samsung Wallet, providing individual access to the same lock while SmartThings helps manage access and automations across the household.  

The collection will be available online in October through The Home Depot, where customers can shop the new ULTRALOQ lineup. The new collection delivers intelligent, effortless and trusted entry across accessible price points, empowering users to choose the access features that best suit their lifestyle and needs.

ULTRALOQ Bolt Mission: The Smart Lock That Knows When You Are Coming Home

Bolt Mission (MSRP: $299.99) delivers a precise, intent-aware hands-free entry experience by combining Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) discovery, UWB ranging, radar-based presence sensing and local decision logic. The result is hands-free entry that responds to true arrival, not strictly proximity. Rather than unlocking simply if a phone is nearby, Bolt Mission analyzes precise distance and direction of approach, allowing it to distinguish an authorized user approaching from outside from normal movement inside the home.

Designed to deliver a premium hands-free experience, users can keep their phone in their pocket or bag while the Xthings Home app runs securely in the background. With Bolt Mission, there's no app to open upon approach, no PIN to enter and no separate hub required for hands-free entry.  

To support dependable intent detection (approach vs. departure) and efficient battery life, Bolt Mission features built-in radar to keep the lock alert when it matters most and conserve power when it does not. Intent detection logic is processed locally between the authorized phone and the lock, delivering fast approach-and-unlock entry.

ULTRALOQ Bolt Pro: Premium Front-Door Deadbolt with Wallet-Based Access 

Bolt Pro (MSRP: $269.99) is the collection's premium digital-key deadbolt, bringing Aliro-Certified tap-to-unlock access together with fingerprint, PIN, app and physical-key entry. Aliro-Certified, Bolt Pro lets users unlock their door with a simple tap of their compatible device, without ever having to open an app. Digital keys are stored in a compatible mobile wallet, giving users a familiar tap experience similar to the contactless interactions they already use every day.

Designed to support a wide range of access methods, Bolt Pro pairs digital wallet access with fingerprint, PIN, app control and physical key backup. While digital wallet access may be ideal for everyday users, fingerprint provides fast personalized entry options and PIN codes can be issued to children, guests, cleaners or other service providers in need of access. 

ULTRALOQ Latch 5 Pro: Wallet-Based Access for More Doors

Latch 5 Pro (MSRP: $249.99) brings the same tap-to-unlock digital wallet experience to doors that use a lever rather than a deadbolt, including side entrances, home offices, garage-entry doors, rentals and shared spaces. Residents or employees can use a compatible digital wallet or fingerprint for access, while visitors and other temporary users can receive PINs. Aliro and Matter Certified, Latch 5 Pro delivers the same digital key experience and smart home platform compatibility as Bolt Pro.
